definition: Comparable in certain respects, often to help explain something.
example: The court considered an analogous case with a similar contractual dispute.
nuance: Analogous does not mean identical; an analogy can illuminate while still having limits.
prompt: A writer compares two systems because they share a useful structural similarity.
options: She described an analogous process in biology to explain the feedback loop in economics.
The systems were analogous because they had nothing relevant in common.
The two words were analogous simply because they rhymed.
She flagged one reading as analogous because it broke every pattern the two systems shared.
reasons: This sentence demonstrates the meaning: comparable in certain respects, often to help explain something.
A shared sound alone does not establish a useful comparison of meaning or structure.
This confuses the word with anomalous, which describes something that departs from a pattern.

practice.prompt: A science teacher wants her students to understand how the heart moves blood.
options: She timed their pulses with the analogous clock that hung above the whiteboard.
A student called the heart analogous to a strawberry because both are red and roughly the same shape.
The heart is simply analogous, so she explained it without comparing it to anything else.
She told the class that the heart is analogous to a pump pushing water through pipes.
reasons: This confuses the word with analog, which describes a clock with hands rather than digits.
Color and shape are surface features that reveal nothing about how a heart works.
A thing can only be analogous to something else, so the word needs a comparison.
A heart and a pump both move fluid, so the comparison makes the organ easier to grasp.
